summary: 52 steps: 7 before the move (2 blocking), 12 to re-create, 4 for the move itself, 23 checks afterwards and 6 to roll back.

phases.title: Before the move: fix the blockers and make the decisions
phases.intro: Everything here is settled while the account is still at its current position. NO-GO steps block the move; REVIEW steps need a decision or a check by hand.

steps.title: SCP Fernhill-EU-Only-Regions / DenyOutsideEU denies 7 actions after the move
steps.detail: Attached at OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu) in the target organization. Allowed today; after the move it denies: athena:StartQueryExecution in us-east-1; ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment in us-east-1; ec2:RunInstances in us-east-1; glue:StartJobRun in us-east-1; kms:Decrypt in us-east-1; s3:GetObject in us-east-1; s3:PutObject in us-east-1. The change to review: edit statement DenyOutsideEU so it no longer covers account 111111111118 (for example a Condition on aws:PrincipalAccount, or a narrower Action or Resource list), detach Fernhill-EU-Only-Regions from OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu), or stop using the actions before the move.
steps.finding: 7 findings with the same cause

aws organizations update-policy --policy-id p-fern0002 --content file://Fernhill-EU-Only-Regions.json

Allowed today; after the move it denies: s3:PutObject by arn:aws:iam::111111111115:role/SettlementExporter in eu-west-1, us-east-1. The change to review: edit statement EnforceOrgIdentities so these principals are exempt (for example list their organization in the aws:PrincipalOrgID condition, or exempt the resource), detach Fernhill-Block-External-Principals from OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu), or move the callers inside the target organization.

steps.title: Make the account able to stand alone
steps.detail: Before it can leave, the account needs its own verified contact information, a payment method and a support plan choice; Organizations fails the removal with ConstraintViolationException until they are in place (with Enterprise Support, a billing case can arrange the standalone period instead of a payment method per account). It then has to be invited by the target management account 222222222221 and accept the invitation: an account belongs to one organization at a time, so it leaves first; the invitation must be answered within 15 days; the policies attached to the target root and the OU it lands in apply at once; the target's organization trail covers it automatically and Config, GuardDuty or Security Hub may be enabled automatically for new members, so account-level trails and detectors may double charges; Organizations does not create OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an invited account. SCPs in the source that deny organizations:LeaveOrganization must be lifted for the move, or the source management account removes the account instead. The account also loses access to the cost and usage data of its time in the source organization and is no longer covered by the source organization's agreements. Transfer procedure model 2026-11-02. Contact information, alternate contacts and the payment method can be checked with the Account API; identity verification and the support plan are done in the console.
steps.where: account larkspur-data-prod (111111111118), signed in as root or an administrator

steps.title: Lift the deny on organizations:LeaveOrganization in SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails / DenyLeaveOrganization, or let the management account remove the account
steps.detail: SCP Larkspur-Baseline-Guardrails (p-lark0001) is attached at root Root (r-lark) and denies organizations:LeaveOrganization without a condition, so leave-organization run from inside the account fails. Either detach the policy or edit the statement for the duration of the move and put it back afterwards, or run remove-account-from-organization from the management account, which SCPs do not restrict.

steps.title: Find what references the 3 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) of the account
steps.detail: When the account leaves the organization, Identity Center cleans up the resources it created in the account; the documentation names the service-linked role, and the IAM roles provisioned for permission sets (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) go with the instance's control over the account, so plan for them to disappear and confirm in IAM after the move. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. List the exact role ARNs now, while they exist, and search for them so the references can be updated after the move.

steps.title: Keep or replace stack StackSet-larkspur-baseline-roles-99ef627b-e471-7169-1578-5f22b2eda054 before StackSet larkspur-baseline-roles deletes it
steps.detail: StackSet larkspur-baseline-roles is service-managed with automatic deployment on and RetainStacksOnAccountRemoval off. When an account is removed from a target organization or OU, StackSets deletes its stack instances and their resources: here AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy x1, AWS::IAM::Role x3. Whatever in the account uses them stops working at that moment, and the resources are not there for a rollback either. Before the move, either turn RetainStacksOnAccountRemoval on for the StackSet (the stack then stays in the account, detached from the StackSet and no longer updated) or make sure the destination deploys an equivalent. Turning retention on is a setting of the whole StackSet and applies to every account that leaves its targets from then on.

phases.title: Before the move: re-create what does not travel
phases.intro: Shares, delegations, permission sets and stacks that are scoped to the account's current position do not follow it. Prepare the replacements now so nothing is interrupted.

steps.title: Re-share larkspur-core-network with the account directly: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
steps.detail: Owner 111111111112 shares larkspur-core-network (ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule) with arn:aws:organizations::111111111111:organization/o-larkspur0001 today. After the move those principals no longer cover the account. Ask the owner to add account 111111111118 as a principal before the move so nothing attached to these resources is interrupted. The account will be outside the organization, so the share has to allow external principals and the account has to accept an invitation. The documentation says traffic or a declared operation stops with this share, so the move stays NO-GO until it is done: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). Potentially affected: ec2:RunInstances in use may target the shared resources; confirm. ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. The account uses ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, which needs the share: that stops working. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.

steps.title: Plan stack data-lake-ingest off the shared networking it references
steps.detail: It references tgw-54924a77a3120b1ad (parameter TransitGatewayId), shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. What the documentation says happens when the share ends: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. The stack owns the attachment: it keeps carrying traffic, but a stack update that replaces it, or redeploying the stack, fails because the account can no longer create attachments to this transit gateway. Redeploying the stack with subnets and attachments the account owns, or that the destination shares with it, is the fix; the parameters named above are where the stack takes them from.

phases.title: The move
phases.intro: Run these in order. Between leaving and accepting the invitation the account is standalone, with no SCPs and no organization features; keep that window short.

steps.title: Invite the account into Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001)
steps.detail: The invitation (a handshake) is valid for 15 days. Send it before the account leaves so the standalone window is short.
commands: aws organizations invite-account-to-organization --target Id=111111111118,Type=ACCOUNT --notes "Move of larkspur-data-prod planned with orgshift"

steps.title: Leave Larkspur Holdings (o-larkspur0001)
steps.detail: Run leave-organization from inside the account, or remove it from the management account (which SCPs do not restrict). Both need the standalone prerequisites to be in place. From this moment no SCP, RCP or tag policy of the source applies, organization-scoped shares stop reaching the account and Identity Center deletes its assignments and roles.
steps.where: account larkspur-data-prod (111111111118), or management account 111111111111 of Larkspur Holdings
commands: aws organizations leave-organization   # run inside the account
aws organizations remove-account-from-organization --account-id 111111111118   # alternative, run by the management account

steps.title: Accept the invitation
steps.detail: The account joins Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) at its root with the AWS managed default policies attached. Everything on the verdict board that applies at the target position applies from the next step on.
commands: aws organizations accept-handshake --handshake-id <handshake ID from the previous command>

steps.title: Move the account from the root to OU Retail (ou-fern-ret)
steps.detail: Until this call the account sits at the target root with only the policies attached there.

phases.title: After the move: checks
phases.intro: Confirm what the simulation predicted and finish what could only be done once the account is at its new position.

steps.title: Confirm the account sits under OU Retail (ou-fern-ret) and the expected policies reach it
steps.detail: The parent must be ou-fern-ret. The policies listed for the account should match the target chain of the simulation (added: SCP Fernhill-Root-Guardrails, SCP Fernhill-EU-Only-Regions, SCP aws-guardrails-kjwqpf, RCP Fernhill-Block-External-Principals, TAG Fernhill-Cost-Allocation, BACKUP Fernhill-Core-Backups).

steps.title: Confirm CloudTrail coverage

steps.title: Enroll the account in Control Tower from Account Factory (OU Retail)
steps.detail: Moving into a registered OU applies the OU's SCPs at once (the 3 preventive guardrail SCP(s) on the chain are attached to the OUs), but the 4 detective control(s) do not report and the baseline is not deployed until the account is enrolled. Enrolment is done from Account Factory (enroll account) and needs an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the account that trusts management account 222222222221, no Config recorder or delivery channel of the account's own in the governed regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), and an email address and name that Account Factory can register. The account has to have joined o-fernhill0001 before it can be enrolled.
steps.where: management account 222222222221 of Fernhill Group (Account Factory)
steps.finding: Target OU Retail is registered with Control Tower; the account has to be enrolled
commands: # Control Tower console → Account Factory → Enroll account → larkspur-data-prod, OU OU Retail (ou-fern-ret)

phases.title: Rollback
phases.intro: If something breaks, this puts the account back where it was. Built from the source policy chain of the simulation.
